title: Tiered fairness-aware SLO and regional eviction playbook
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Problem: current SLO work at Redwood is strong on per-endpoint latency/availability but lacks a coherent approach for guaranteeing cross-tenant fairness during multi-region failover and emergency capacity reclamation. This ticket defines a reproducible taxonomy for per-endpoint and per-model SLIs, an error-budget accounting model that preserves fairness-weighted allocations, and operational circuit breaker / load-shedding policies that can be automated by the routing layer. The deliverable will be a playbook and automation spec that runtime, routing, and console teams can implement and test.
goals: Define canonical SLI surface for model endpoints (availability, p95/p99 latency, quality SLI for deterministic prompts)
Create an error budget accounting model that supports weighted tenant fairness during regional failover and capacity shortfalls
Specify adaptive circuit breaker thresholds tied to weighted burn-rate rather than raw QPS
Design priority-aware load-shedding algorithm that enforces tenant fairness; include tenant weights, route tiers, and pinned-variant protections
Produce a step-by-step playbook for failover, eviction, and reconciliation including automated rollbacks and observability hooks
Deliver tests, dashboards, and an initial runtime prototype to validate behavior under synthetic surge scenarios
definitions: Weighted Availability SLI: availability measured per-tenant and aggregated with tenant weight factors (weight derived from commitment tier + customer SLA + recent error-budget health)
Quality SLI: model output quality measured via automated evals on a canonical promptset linked to endpoint rollout; reported as pass-rate or semantic similarity percentile
Fairness Score: a normalized metric (0..1) representing deviation from target allocation during under-capacity events; 0 = perfect fairness, >0 indicates deviation
Burn-Rate: rate at which an endpoint/model is consuming error budget relative to expected baseline; used for circuit-breaker gating
Eviction Slice: an atomic unit of traffic removal (e.g., percentage of QPS or pinned variant fraction) applied per tenant/route to meet aggregate SLO targets
decision_log: 2025-02-19: Agreed to use tenant-weighted aggregation for availability SLOs instead of simple tenant-count averaging (decision by Reliability WG)
2025-02-22: Chose burn-rate driven circuit breakers (thresholds expressed as multiples of allowed burn-rate) to reduce noisy QPS thresholds
2025-02-26: Opted to protect pinned model variants and admin routes from automatic eviction unless explicit emergency mode is enabled
2025-03-01: Decided to include a soft-eviction phase (graceful throttling with client-visible headers) before hard-eviction to aid client-side degradation handling

acceptance_criteria: Canonical SLI document published with worked examples for at least three endpoint archetypes
Simulator demonstrates that the fairness-aware eviction algorithm reduces max tenant deviation by >= 30% vs baseline in 5 synthetic scenarios
Routing layer can produce eviction recommendations and circuit-breaker triggers in staging based on burn-rate signals
Dashboards surface live fairness score and per-tenant burn-rate; alerts fire when fairness score > 0.2
Playbook includes automated rollback criteria and a validated testing checklist
Peer review approvals from Runtime, Routing, Console, and SRE owners
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (docs + simulation): publish SLI taxonomy and run sims in isolation (Week 1-2)
Phase 1 (staging integration): wire routing hints and burn-rate signals to a staging routing cluster; run chaos experiments with controlled region loss (Week 3)
Phase 2 (limited canary): enable soft-eviction and advisory circuit breakers for 10% of traffic on low-risk endpoints; monitor fairness score and rollback if needed (Week 4)
Phase 3 (production): enable active eviction automation for non-pinned routes with enforced governance and audit logs (Week 5-6)
Post-launch (observability): 30-day measurement window and retrospective; adjust tenant weights and thresholds based on empirical burn-rate curves
monitoring_and_alerting: Metrics to emit: tenant_weighted_availability, tenant_error_budget_remaining, tenant_burn_rate, fairness_score, eviction_events_count, circuit_breaker_state
SLO alerts: firing when tenant_weighted_availability < target for >5m OR fairness_score > 0.2 for >10m
Operational alert: circuit_breaker enters forced-open state in >2 regions simultaneously
Audit logs: every eviction decision must include timestamp, triggering signal, affected tenants with pre/post allocations, and operator id if manual
Dashboards: heatmap of tenant deviation by region and time; chart overlay of burn-rate vs capacity utilization
open_questions: How should tenant weight be calibrated for newly onboarded customers with no historical usage? (cold-start weight policy)
What maximum preemption percentage should be allowed for mid-tier customers before manual approval is required?
Do we expose fairness_score to customers or only surface it internally?
What's the canonical TTL for error-budget transfers between regional pools during failover?
Should quality SLI degradation be allowed to trade off with latency/availability in certain route tiers?
